source.citation: Thompson, D'Arcy W. (1917) On Growth and Form. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. Ch. XVII, pp. 769, Fig. 403 (scapulae after Dwight).

claim_text: Human scapulae of differing form (after Dwight) are comparable/transformable by the coordinate method.

quotes.text: Fig. 403. Human scapulae (after Dwight). A, Caucasian; B, Negro; C, North American Indian (from Kentucky Mountains).
The regularity of the succession of 'transformations' is striking; but the differences are no greater than we may find between individuals of a single race.

model.name: Thompson-Dwight coordinate method on human scapula outlines

state_variables.x: reference coordinates on the Caucasian scapula (form A, Cartesian grid in Fig. 403)
state_variables.phi(x): image coordinates of x on a second scapula form (B or C) under Dwight's deformed grid
state_variables.t: interpolation parameter along A -> target (1 = full coordinate warp to B or C)

equations.formula: phi : R^2 -> R^2 orientation-preserving, phi(grid_A) = grid_B

equations.source: equidistant / linear morph along the transformation

equations.formula: affine special case phi(x) = A x + b

boundary_conditions.forms: A Caucasian baseline Cartesian grid; B Negro; C North American Indian (Dwight)
boundary_conditions.view: costal surface / outline as drawn in Fig. 403

parameter_regime.controls: arc-length semilandmarks per scapula border segment

empirical_claims.claim: Forms B and C are obtainable from A by a coordinate transformation.
empirical_claims.test: TPS warp of A matches drawn B/C better than copying A (Procrustes, IoU)

empirical_claims.claim: Inter-racial differences are within individual variation of one race.
empirical_claims.reason: requires population sample beyond Dwight's three panels; not pinned here

digitisation.primary_surface: Fig. 403 on p. 769 (leaf n788): three stacked scapula outlines with coordinate grids
digitisation.segmentation: grayscale, ink threshold < 140, morphological closing/opening, three largest components top-to-bottom = A, B, C

specimen_photograph.organism: Homo sapiens (human scapula, archaeological specimen with sun bleaching)
specimen_photograph.use: descriptive bone-vs-background CV segmentation only; not used for the Fig. 403 verdict
